points.what: APAC was the top regional driver of the week's order growth, contributing 17 orders, 141.7% of the total change.
points.so_what: Order growth this week depended heavily on a single region.

points.what: North America contributed -18 orders, -150.0% of the week's total change, the largest negative contributor of any region.
points.so_what: The North America pullback offset most of the gains elsewhere and limited total order growth to 1.6%.

points.what: Search was the top traffic-source driver, contributing 17 orders, 141.7% of the week's total change, while Facebook contributed -14 orders, -116.7%.
points.so_what: Order growth relied heavily on Search to cover a pullback from Facebook rather than adding net new growth.

points.what: AOV was $86.1, up 1.1% WoW and up 3.2% YoY.
points.so_what: Revenue growth this week is coming from both more orders and slightly bigger baskets, not one or the other alone.

points.what: The cancellation rate fell to 12.7%, down 2.8 pp WoW, a notable move, and down 4.2 pp YoY.
points.so_what: A lower cancellation rate reduces the share of orders lost to cancellation, supporting the week's revenue.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of Feb 16 2026 was 9.0%, down 1.0 pp WoW, a notable move, and down 2.3 pp YoY.
points.so_what: A lower return rate for that week means fewer of its orders came back within 14 days, a favorable read on order quality.

points.what: New signups reached 260, up 12.6% WoW, a notable move, and up 15.6% YoY, compared with order growth of 1.6% WoW.
points.so_what: New-account growth is running well ahead of order growth this week.

summary.headline: Behind target on orders (88.7%) and revenue (94.7%) this week, with the quarter and year also behind at 92.0% attainment.

points.what: Orders reached 743, up 1.6% WoW, but that was only 88.7% of the weekly target, a gap of 95 orders.
points.so_what: Growth was not enough to close the weekly order target gap.

points.what: Revenue reached $55,878, up 6.1% WoW, at 94.7% of the weekly target, a gap of $3,107.
points.so_what: Revenue attainment was closer to target than orders but still finished short.

points.what: QTD and YTD revenue attainment both stand at 92.0%, with the quarter behind target and 3 weeks left in Q1.
points.so_what: Both the quarter and the year remain behind target heading into the final stretch.

points.what: Orders grew 59.1% YoY and revenue grew 72.6% YoY, both below the 75% growth the 2026 targets assume.
points.so_what: Year-over-year growth trailing the assumed pace helps explain why attainment stays under 100%.

points.what: Weekly orders attainment was 88.7% (gap of 95 orders) and weekly revenue attainment was 94.7% (gap of $3,107).
points.so_what: Both KPIs finished the week behind target.

points.what: QTD revenue attainment is 92.0%, with $231,662 remaining to the full-quarter target and 3 weeks left in Q1.
points.so_what: Closing the quarter gap requires stronger weeks than achieved so far this quarter.

points.what: YTD revenue attainment is 92.0%, and the required weekly run-rate for the rest of the year is $77,812 versus a recent 8-week run-rate of $54,024.
points.so_what: The recent pace is well below what is needed to reach the full-year target.

points.what: QTD revenue attainment is 92.0%, behind target, with $231,662 still needed and only 3 weeks left in the quarter.
points.so_what: Reaching the quarter target requires stronger weeks than the recent pace has delivered.

points.what: The full-year required weekly revenue run-rate is $77,812, well above the current 8-week run-rate of $54,024.
points.so_what: At the recent pace, the full-year revenue target is out of reach.

points.what: Every month so far this year, Jan, Feb, and Mar (MTD), has finished behind target, with none ahead.
points.so_what: The revenue shortfall has persisted across the quarter, not just in this single week.
